name: Replace poles (planned pole replacement)
summary: Wood poles that fail inspection or strength testing are replaced in a planned program of about 325 to 350 poles a year. After a site check and locates, a crew of three line technicians and an apprentice sets the new pole beside the old one, moves the wires and equipment across under a work protection permit or reclose hold-off, and pulls the old pole if nothing else is on it. On most urban poles telecom and cable companies still have lines on the old pole, so the crew leaves a topped stub and the joint-use technologist sends transfer notices. The crew work takes hours, but the case stays open for months while attachers move their cables and a crew returns to pull the stub.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 346,000 customers, about 49,000 poles and 20 in-house line crews.
baseline.notes: Planned replacements only; poles broken by storms or vehicle collisions are replaced through outage restoration and major event response.

trigger: Work scheduling releases a pole replacement work order, raised from a condemned pole in inspection or testing, to an overhead crew.
end_state: The new pole is in service, the old pole or stub has been removed, crew time is approved and the pole record has gone to records; or the pole is found not to need replacing.

volume.seasonality: Fewer from December to March when frozen ground slows digging; more from May to November.

evidence.note: 325 to 350 poles a year through planned work in a normal year (source), about 27 to 29 a month.

surge.cause: follow-up after a major storm (temporary repairs made permanent, stubs and leaning poles)

evidence.note: About 400 poles to repair or replace after the May 2022 storm (source); those were replaced as emergency restoration, so the surge here covers only the planned follow-up work, the author's estimate. The organisation file's multiplier of up to 40 counts the storm replacements themselves.

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Ontario One Call member portal and locate management
SCADA for stations and feeder devices
Time entry for crews and staff

resources.name: Overhead line crew (three to four line trades with a bucket truck and a digger)
Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Review the pole replacement order
steps.description: The overhead lines supervisor opens the pole replacement work order in the ERP and mobile tool, reads the inspection or pole test result that condemned the pole, the pole number, height and class and the attached equipment, and assigns it to a crew lead.

error.defect_description: Wrong pole number carried from the inspection record.

evidence.note: Poles are condemned by the critical pole testing program (source); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the pole site
steps.description: The supervisor drives to the pole, confirms its condition and number, checks whether a digger derrick can reach it or it sits in a rear lot, notes telecom and other attachments, transformers and services, and picks the spot for the new hole beside the old pole.

error.defect_description: Rear-lot access or an attachment is missed.

next.condition: rear-lot or private property pole needs access arranged
pole found serviceable or already replaced after a collision

evidence.note: Roadside versus rear-lot access drives the work (source); shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Arrange access with property owners
steps.description: The work planner sends letters or door hangers to the owners of the yards the crew must enter, asks them to unlock gates, keep pets in and clear items, and arranges any fence removal or hedge trimming before the crew day.

error.defect_description: Owner not reached; crew finds a locked gate or dog.

evidence.note: Notice before crews enter backyards (source); timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit a locate request
steps.description: The work planner enters the new hole location and any anchor on the Ontario One Call portal with the planned dig date and files the ticket number on the job.

error.defect_description: Dig area marked too small.

control.basis: Ontario Underground Infrastructure Notification System Act, 2012 and Occupational Health and Safety Act: locate all buried plant before excavating

steps.name: Wait for underground owners to mark the site
steps.description: The utility's own locators and the gas, telecom and municipal owners mark their buried plant around the pole within five business days, or clear the request.

error.defect_description: A buried service is mismarked.

steps.name: Stage the pole and hardware
steps.description: A stores attendant issues the pole of the right height and class from the pole yard, with crossarms, insulators, guys and connectors, against the work order, and loads the pole trailer for the crew.

error.defect_description: Wrong pole class or missing hardware.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Request switching or a hold-off
steps.description: The work planner sends the control room the job date, crew and protection holder, asking either for isolation and a planned outage (heavy framing, transformers) or for a reclose hold-off so the crew can work the lines live with rubber gloves and cover-up.

error.defect_description: Wrong device on the request.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the switching order or hold-off plan
steps.description: A switching and outage planner checks the feeder in the GIS and outage system, writes the switching steps or the hold-off on the upstream recloser, books any outage and triggers customer notices.

error.defect_description: Isolation point or recloser wrong.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit or reclose hold-off issued by the control room before work on or near energized lines

evidence.note: Wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold for the booked crew day
steps.description: The pole waits for a slot in the crew schedule, often grouped with other poles on the same street. The day before, the supervisor confirms crew, digger derrick, bucket truck, pole and weather.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: weather, frozen ground, truck breakdown or emergency work

evidence.note: Planned poles are fitted around capital and trouble work; postponement share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Reschedule the pole
steps.description: The work planner rebooks the crew day, moves the switching order and outage notice, and re-sends access notices for rear-lot poles.

error.defect_description: Owner not told of the new date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive the crew, pole and trucks to site
steps.description: The crew tows the pole trailer behind the digger derrick and drives the bucket truck from the operations centre to the pole.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold the tailboard and set up
steps.description: The crew lead runs the pre-job briefing and hazard assessment, sets traffic control or ground mats in a yard, places the trucks, and covers up energized conductors near the work.

error.defect_description: A hazard is not recorded or discussed.

control.basis: Electrical Utility Safety Rules (IHSA) and Ontario Regulation 213/91: pre-job hazard assessment, limits of approach, traffic protection

evidence.note: Ground mats in yards (mb_pole); duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take work protection or hold-off from the control room
steps.description: The system operator either directs switching and issues a work protection permit, after which the crew tests and grounds the line, or places a reclose hold-off for live-line work and confirms it to the crew lead.

error.defect_description: Hold-off placed on the wrong device.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit or reclose hold-off issued by the control room before work on or near energized lines

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Dig the hole and set the new pole
steps.description: The crew augers the new hole beside the old pole with the digger derrick, about ten percent of the pole length plus two feet deep, lifts and plumbs the new pole, backfills and tamps it. Rear-lot poles are dug and raised with smaller equipment and by hand.

error.defect_description: Pole not plumb or set too shallow.

evidence.note: Setting depth from ho_maint; 2-3 hours roadside and 4-6 hours rear-lot for the whole change (entergy_poles), split here between setting and transfer.

steps.name: Assist as groundman
steps.description: The apprentice works on the ground alongside the journeypersons: rigging the pole, guiding the butt into the hole, tamping backfill, and sending up hardware and tools.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Four-person crew with one apprentice, as in the organisation file; runs alongside the pole setting.

steps.name: Transfer conductors and equipment
steps.description: From the bucket, the journeypersons frame the new pole, move the primary and secondary conductors, transformer, cut-outs, services and street light, and transfer grounds and guys. Customers fed from the pole see a brief outage while their wires move.

error.defect_description: A service or ground connection left loose.

evidence.note: Brief outage while wires move (mb_pole); duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Release protection or hold-off
steps.description: The crew removes grounds and cover-up and surrenders the permit or hold-off; the system operator restores the normal configuration and confirms customers are back on.

error.defect_description: Outage system not updated.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit or reclose hold-off issued by the control room before work on or near energized lines

next.condition: no telecom or third-party cables on the old pole
telecom or other attachers still on the old pole

evidence.note: Share of poles with attachers is the author's estimate for an urban and suburban system.

steps.name: Pull the old pole
steps.description: With nothing left on it, the crew cuts any remaining hardware, pulls the old pole with the digger derrick, fills the old hole and loads the pole for disposal.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Top the old pole and leave the stub
steps.description: The crew cuts the old pole off above the highest telecom attachment, caps it and tags it, leaving a stub pole carrying the telecom and cable TV lines until the owners move them to the new pole.

error.defect_description: Stub not tagged or recorded, so it is forgotten.

evidence.note: Old pole removal delayed when telecommunication wires are present (source).

steps.name: Send transfer notices to the attachers
steps.description: The joint-use design technologist emails each telecom and cable company on the stub pole a transfer notice with the pole number, location and date the new pole was set, and logs the open transfer in the joint-use spreadsheet.

error.defect_description: Notice sent to the wrong attacher or not logged.

evidence.note: Joint use sits with design technologists in the organisation file's ae-joint-use process; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for attachers to move their cables
steps.description: Each telecom and cable company schedules its own crew to move its lines to the new pole. Several companies may be on one pole, each working on its own timetable, so the stub can stand for months.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Stub poles standing for months are a known problem (organisation file); a two-week to six-month range (mode about a month) is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase overdue transfers
steps.description: The joint-use technologist checks the open transfer list, emails or calls the attacher's coordinator with the overdue pole list and escalates long-standing stubs, then waits for the attacher's crew.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Return and remove the stub pole
steps.description: Once the transfer is confirmed, a two-person crew is scheduled as fill-in work, drives out, pulls the stub with the digger derrick, fills the hole and hauls the stub away.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Stub removal is low-priority fill-in work; times include travel and are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Clean up and request site restoration
steps.description: The crew rakes out spoil, tops up the hole with fill, removes mats and debris, puts back any fence section and logs lawn or asphalt restoration for the contractor.

error.defect_description: Restoration not requested, prompting a customer complaint.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the work order and redlines
steps.description: The crew lead records the new pole's height, class, treatment and year, the removed pole, hours by work order and material used in the mobile tool and on the drawing.

error.defect_description: Pole data or hours missing or wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and sign off the job
steps.description: The supervisor reviews the hours, the pole record and the hazard assessment, approves the timesheets and signs the job complete, or sends it back for missing data.

error.defect_description: A wrong charge is approved.

control.basis: Collective agreement and payroll policy: supervisor approval of crew time

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the work order and send the as-built
steps.description: The work planner sets the work order to complete in the ERP and sends the pole record and redline to the project manager and records for the GIS and fixed asset update.

error.defect_description: Record attached to the wrong pole.

next.condition: pole replaced and old pole gone

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Rear-lot pole
exceptions.description: The pole sits in a back yard; owners are notified, gates and fences arranged, and the crew works with smaller equipment and by hand.

exceptions.name: Stub pole left for attachers
exceptions.description: Telecom or cable lines remain on the old pole; the crew tops it, notices go out and a crew returns months later to pull the stub.

exceptions.name: Overdue attacher transfer
exceptions.description: An attacher has not moved its lines and the joint-use technologist chases and escalates.

exceptions.name: Weather or crew postponement
exceptions.description: Weather, frozen ground or emergency work cancels the crew day.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from release to the crew until the old pole is gone and the job is closed
benchmarks.population: Ontario municipal distributor planned pole replacements, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about four to six weeks to the new pole in service, plus months of attacher transfers on about two thirds of poles. No published distributor figure was found.

benchmarks.unit: hours on site for the pole change
benchmarks.population: Residential distribution poles, roadside (2-3 h) and rear-lot (4-6 h)

evidence.note: US utility figures used as an outside reference.

benchmarks.unit: poles per year through planned work

pain_points.description: Stub poles stand for months while each telecom and cable company moves its lines on its own schedule, and the utility must chase transfers and send a second crew.

evidence.note: Old pole removal delayed when telecom wires are present (source); duration is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Rear-lot poles need owner access, hand digging and longer crew time.
Open transfers are tracked in a spreadsheet, so stubs are forgotten when a notice is not logged.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: An in-depth look at Hydro Ottawa's grid maintenance
sources.supports: Critical pole program tests thousands of poles a year; replacements are driven by testing or by emergencies such as vehicle collisions; cable replacements are prioritised from fault histories, cable tests and estimated life; new cable goes in 4-inch PVC or HDPE conduit.

sources.title: Contractors: locates and safe digging
sources.supports: Locate requests at least five business days before digging (ten for multi-address requests), legally required; hand digging or hydrovac near cables; stay 1.5 m from marked cables; re-locate when marks expire. Current page; the five-business-day rule applied in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa restores power to 94 per cent of customers - 2:00 PM update
sources.supports: About 400 poles to repair or replace after the May 2022 storm, against 325 to 350 poles replaced through planned work in a normal year; nearly a year's construction done in nine days.

sources.title: No two poles are the same
sources.supports: Roadside residential pole replacement 2 to 3 hours, rear-lot or alley 4 to 6 hours, with a line crew of four or five and a bucket truck with auger; steps: clear equipment, remove old pole, dig hole avoiding underground lines, set new pole, reconnect.

sources.title: What to expect with pole replacement
sources.supports: Customers notified ahead of time, and again before crews enter backyards; gates, pets and fencing; ground mats; brief outage while wires move to the new pole; removal of the old pole may be delayed by ground conditions or telecommunication wires.

sources.title: Keys to the Utility Work Protection Code
sources.publisher: Infrastructure Health and Safety Association (IHSA) Health and Safety Magazine, vol. 23 issue 2
sources.supports: The Electrical Utility Safety Rules govern worker conduct near hazards; the Utility Work Protection Code uses permits and tags to show when lines are safe to work on; issuers and workers must be trained and certified.

sources.title: Wages: Lineworker - Electrical Power Systems in Ontario (NOC 72203)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wage low 29.70, median 49.48, high 62.90; Ottawa region 32.93, 50.63, 63.29 (2024-2025 reference period).

assumptions: One case is one pole, open until the old pole or stub is removed; in practice the replacement work order is often closed when the new pole is in service and stub removal is tracked as a separate order, which would shorten the measured cycle to about five weeks.
About 65% of poles carry telecom or cable attachments that must be moved by their owners.
Every pole job takes either a work protection permit or a reclose hold-off from the control room.
Crew work is recorded as elapsed crew time with people = 3 journeypersons plus a concurrent apprentice step during pole setting.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).

The simulated median (about 95 to 100 days) is slightly above the 90-day benchmark estimate; both rest on the attacher-transfer wait, which has no published figure for this distributor and dominates the cycle.
Storm-broken poles are outside this workflow; the surge covers planned follow-up work only.
